title: Federal Judge Bars Trump Administration from Threatening Election Workers Over California Ballots
summary: A federal judge issued an order preventing the Trump administration's Justice Department from threatening or coercing election workers in California, marking another legal setback for efforts to assert control over local elections.
contents: A federal judge delivered a significant blow to the Trump administration's efforts to assert control over local election processes. The judge issued a sweeping order barring the Justice Department from threatening or coercing election workers tasked with processing California ballots. The ruling represents an escalation of judicial intervention in election administration, protecting workers from pressure campaigns originating from federal authorities. The decision reflects ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and state and local election officials over control of electoral processes. Election workers had faced mounting pressure from federal government pressure campaigns seeking to halt ballot processing. The judicial order establishes a legal boundary preventing such federal interference in local election operations. This ruling follows a pattern of court decisions constraining the administration's attempts to influence state and local election procedures.

## Event Report

🇮🇷🚚 Iran Keeps Military Supplies Coming Despite US Sanctions Iran has imported at least $2B in equipment, explosives and heavy trucks since January 2025 through more than 5,000 defense-linked agencies, according to Reuters investigation. Supplies kept arriving during the war, complicating US efforts to starve Iranian missile and drone factories of materials. The buyers operate under numbered names beginning with MOD, short for Ministry of Defense. Most date to 2013, meaning Iran had years to build these channels before the fighting began. Despite decades of sanctions against Iran’s military, Reuters found no evidence that the numbered agencies it examined occurred themselves on Western sanctions lists. Oil sales help pay the bills, with intermediaries and foreign shell companies using revenue held abroad to buy goods and send them home. For 97% of the shipments, the records showed settlement without a currency transfer. Keeping the money overseas reduces the need for cross-border payments that can trigger sanctions checks. One buyer, MOD 346428, brought in rocket propellants, explosives, weapons components and heavy trucks between January 2025 and June 2026. These represent the less photogenic essentials behind a missile launch: fuel, parts and vehicles that could carry launch equipment. Deliveries came by land, sea and air, with much of the cargo listed as originating in China, Russia and Germany. A naval blockade cannot close every road or air route, and a product’s country of origin does not prove its manufacturer knowingly supplied Iran’s military. Reuters examined bank records, corporate filings and import data, cross-checking part of some 19,000 import records. Many goods also have civilian uses, so a shipment of components cannot occur counted as a batch of finished missiles. The records do not establish whether Iran represents replacing weapons as fast as it fires them. The US Treasury told Reuters it occurred “10 steps ahead,” a confident assessment for an enforcement effort still watching supplies get through. The findings show how Iran has kept buying despite restrictions, even if they do not show that sanctions leave it unscathed. Iran’s continued access to military supplies exposes the gap between US pressure and US control. Sanctions and a naval blockade have failed to seal off its procurement network, leaving Iran able to bring in materials for weapons production even during the war. @NewRulesGeo❗Follow us on X

title: PLA military activity detected around Taiwan: 13 sorties, 7 PLAN vessels cross median line
summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported detection of 13 PLA aircraft sorties, 7 PLAN vessels, and 2 official ships operating around Taiwan as of 6 a.m. UTC+8 on October 31, 2026. Six of the 13 aircraft sorties crossed the median line and entered Taiwan's northern, central, and southwestern ADIZ.
contents: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported on October 31, 2026 the detection of significant Chinese military activity in the Taiwan Strait region. A total of 13 People's Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft sorties operated around Taiwan, accompanied by 7 People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) vessels and 2 official ships. Monitoring continued until 6 a.m. local time (UTC+8). Of the 13 aircraft sorties, 6 crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait and entered Taiwan's air defense identification zone (ADIZ) across the island's northern, central, and southwestern sectors. The Republic of China (ROC) Armed Forces maintained continuous monitoring throughout the period. The activity represents routine Chinese military operational patterns in the Taiwan Strait, with aircraft incursions into Taiwan's ADIZ and naval vessels operating in the strategic waterway. Taiwan's defense establishment documented and reported the activity as part of its standard intelligence assessment procedures.

title: Canada's central labour union refuses to handle military cargo destined for Israel
summary: The Canadian Labour Congress, representing approximately 3 million workers, voted to refuse handling weapons and military equipment destined for Israel and called on the Canadian government to end all arms transfers.
contents: After a landmark vote on Thursday, Canada's central labour union, representing some 3 million workers across the country, announced that it would refuse to handle weapons and military equipment destined for Israel. The union demanded the government of Canada take the same action and end all direct and indirect transfers of arms and military equipment to Israel. The Canadian Labour Congress statement emphasized Canada's responsibility to ensure weapons and military equipment produced domestically do not contribute to harm of Palestinian civilians or violations of international humanitarian law. The labour movement rejected all forms of hatred and discrimination, including antisemitism, anti-Palestinian racism and Islamophobia. Commercial data revealed shipments continued and accelerated via indirect routes such as through the United States. An analysis by the Palestinian Youth Movement and partner groups documented more than 390 shipments from 21 Canadian manufacturers in six cities, including over 420,000 bullets, 735 cartridge parts, F-35 jet components such as navigation sensors and radar systems, and dual-use items like GPS antennas. The Canadian Labour Congress maintained decades-long ties with Israel's Histradut trade union but voted in May to cut those ties. The move received support from labour activists and advocacy groups emphasizing Canadian workers' historical role in supporting liberation movements and opposing conflict.
